title: Nadab and Abihu
lead: Aaron's two oldest sons, who saw God on Sinai (Exodus 24:9–11) and died when they brought "strange fire" before the LORD at the tabernacle's inauguration (Leviticus 10:1–2). Their deaths frame the Day of Atonement law and became a classic warning about approaching the holy.

sections.b: Nadab and Abihu are named among Aaron's four sons (Exodus 6:23) and among the leaders invited up Sinai who saw God and ate and drank (Exodus 24:1, 9–11). Their deaths are told in Leviticus 10:1–7 and recalled at the start of the Day of Atonement law (Leviticus 16:1), in the lists of Aaron's descendants (Numbers 3:2–4; 26:60–61) and in Chronicles, which notes they died before their father and had no sons, so the priesthood passed through Eleazar and Ithamar (1 Chronicles 24:1–2). Their story is often read beside Korah's rebels, burned while offering incense (Numbers 16:35), and Uzzah, struck for touching the ark (2 Samuel 6:6–7).
